answer: A falconer's licence names one bird, and the mews record logs every moult and every jess change for that bird's life. A fable falcon bought from a dealer fails the record. At the lagoon of the inspection the jesses must match the falconer's own stitch, and a bought bird wears another man's work. Faking a falcon means keeping a bird for two seasons, bribing a falconer and paying 13,700, and the jade entry in the mews book follows the bird, so a second falcon claiming the same licence is seized.
